pages.text: $(thing)Clay$() is a handy and balanced material for pottery, but hard to find at first. It is usually under grass, in two kinds of place. Where the $(l:core_mechanics/climate#rainfall)annual rainfall$() is at least 175 mm, clay lies in patches everywhere, often marked by certain $(thing)plants$().

pages.name: Clay Indicators
pages.text: Clay, and one of the plants that may show it.

Clay is betrayed by $(thing)Goldenrod$(), $(thing)Perovskia$(), $(thing)Canna$(), $(thing)Water Canna$(), $(thing)Pampas Grass$() and $(thing)Athyrium Fern$() growing close to it. There is also clay in small beds by water: rivers, lakes, ponds.$(br2)Clay can be knapped like stone, with five pieces in hand. If you err, you can close the screen, reshape the clay and try again.
The knapping screen.

The small vessel is the first thing to make. Like all pottery it must be fired before use. Firing heats the item until the clay becomes hard $(thing)ceramic$(): 850 °C. Early on that is done in a $(l:getting_started/pit_kiln)Pit Kiln$(). Ware of $(l:metalworking/fire_clay)Fire Clay$() needs 1300 °C instead.
pages.title: Small Vessel

pages.text: Knapping a small vessel.
The $(l:food/decay#large_vessels)Large Vessel$() is knapped the same way. It can be set down as a block and holds nine stacks. The linked chapter says more.
pages.title: Large Vessel

pages.text: Knapping a large vessel.

Another useful piece is the $(thing)Jug$(). It picks up and $(thing)drinks$() liquids such as fresh water. $(item)$(k:key.use)$() it on the liquid in the world, then use it to drink. It holds $(thing)$(cfg:jugCapacity)$() of liquid.
pages.title: Jug

pages.text: Knapping a jug.
Clay also makes $(thing)Molds$(). Molten metal poured into a mold sets into its shape. Use the mold to take out the item, and sometimes the mold too. The simplest is the ingot mold, shown next.
pages.title: Molds

pages.text: Knapping an ingot mold.
Fire the mold like any clay ware at 850 °C, likely in a $(l:getting_started/pit_kiln)Pit Kiln$(). Then pour metal in, and take it out when it has cooled enough.
The next pages show knapping patterns for several tools.
pages.title: Casting

pages.text: A $(l:metalworking/prospecting#propick)Prospector's Pick$() is the tool for finding rich ore.
A $(thing)Pickaxe$(): the everyday mining tool.
A $(thing)Saw$() is needed for fine wooden parts, such as a $(thing)Workbench$() and many other devices, $(l:core_mechanics/support_beams)Supports$() among them.
A $(thing)Scythe$() cuts plants and leaves in a 3x3x3 area.
A $(l:metalworking/chisel)Chisel$() smooths blocks and carves many decorative ones.
An $(thing)Axe$() for felling trees. A stone axe is worse than a metal one.
A $(thing)Hammer$() is needed for making and working $(l:metalworking/anvils)Anvils$().
A $(thing)Knife$() is a weapon and a cutter of plants.
A $(thing)Hoe$() tills and tends $(l:food/crops)Crops$().
A $(thing)Shovel$() for digging.
